Belarus' membership in the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) has impacted its trade relationships outside of the union in several ways.

Firstly, the EAEU provides preferential treatment to member states in terms of trade. This includes the elimination of most customs duties, the establishment of uniform customs duties for goods imported from outside the union, as well as the coordination of trade policies and regulations. Therefore, Belarusian goods entering the EAEU member states benefit from reduced tariffs and other trade barriers, making them more competitive in these markets.

On the other hand, Belarus' trade relationships with countries outside the EAEU have been impacted by the union's common external tariff. The EAEU's tariff structure is designed to protect domestic industries and limit competition from outside the union. This can make it more difficult for non-member countries to access EAEU markets and make their exports less competitive compared to goods produced within the union. This might mean Belarusian exporters might feel less pressure to adapt to different standards when exporting within the EAEU, however, these differences will become problematic when attempting to export to non-EAEU markets.

Another way the EAEU has affected Belarusian trade relationships outside of the union is that it has sparked trade tensions with some non-member countries, such as Ukraine, which suspended its free trade agreement with the EAEU in 2015. Additionally, the EAEU has been criticized by some Western countries for its close ties with Russia and its perceived lack of transparency.

In summary, Belarus' membership in the EAEU has had both positive and negative impacts on its trade relationships outside of the union. While the EAEU has made it easier for Belarus to trade with member states, it has also created challenges for trade with non-member countries.
